Where it began

Virat Kohli was born in Delhi on 5 November 1988 and grew up in Uttam Nagar, in the west of the city. His family say he was already reaching for a bat at the age of three and asking his father to bowl to him. Bowlers around the world would come to know the feeling.

In 1998 he joined the new West Delhi Cricket Academy under the coach Rajkumar Sharma, and the runs came quickly through the Delhi age-group sides. In 2008 he captained India to victory at the Under-19 World Cup in Malaysia.

The player

His Test debut came against the West Indies in June 2011. The longest format took a little while to warm to him, but his first Test hundred arrived at Adelaide in January 2012 and the floodgates opened. When he took over as full-time Test captain in Australia, he made centuries in each of his first three innings in charge.

He played 123 Tests, scoring 9,230 runs at 46.85 with 30 hundreds and a best of 254 not out. That puts him 15th among all Test cricketers for hundreds, and he held 121 catches besides. As captain he led India in 68 Tests and won 40 of them, and in 2018 he took India to their first Test series win in Australia. He also became the first batsman to make double hundreds in four Test series in a row. He stepped away from Test cricket in May 2025, aged 36.

What made him special

Kohli built his innings along the ground. The cover drive was his favourite stroke and the flick off his pads was nearly as good, played with quick feet and strong wrists. He loved a target to aim at, and he was a master at keeping the score ticking with ones and twos. He was also among the fittest cricketers of his generation and a sharp, safe fielder.

If he had a soft spot, it lay just outside off stump. Bowlers spent years trying to tempt him with the ball that leaves the bat, and now and then it worked. Most days, though, it simply meant more balls for him to drive.

Away from the middle

He has the Arjuna Award, the Padma Shri and the Khel Ratna, and Wisden named him the leading cricketer in the world three years running. Time put him on its list of the hundred most influential people in 2018. Delhi named a stand after him at his home ground.

He is married to the actress Anushka Sharma, and the pair are among the best-known couples in India. After leaving Tests he carried on in one-day cricket for India and in the IPL with Bengaluru.

And finally

For all his records, one prize kept him waiting. He played 18 seasons for Bengaluru before the franchise won its first IPL title in 2025. Then, as if to make up for lost time, they won it again the next year. Patience, it turns out, was the one stroke he had to learn the long way.
